title_as_printed: The differential vapor pressure (dP, in psi) for NaCl, KCl, and CaCl2 solutions at vapor saturated conditions from 200 C to 350 C
pressure_note: Differential pressure dP (psi), measured with differential Bourdon-tube gauges or strain-gauge transducer by comparing the solution (low-pressure, brine side) against pure water at the same temperature; the gauges are 'psid'. Table title: 'differential vapor pressure (dP, in psi) ... at vapor saturated conditions'. Not an absolute vapor pressure; pure-water vapor pressure at T is not tabulated (the text cites Keenan and Keyes 1936). dP is water vapor pressure minus solution vapor pressure (sign taken from the gauge arrangement: brine side fed to the Bourdon tube, water side to the case; the paper's wording establishes dP = P_water - P_brine (water side high-pressure, brine side low-pressure, same T)).

value.what: differential vapor pressure P0(water) - P(solution), authors' wording: differential vapor pressure

P.what: vapor-saturated conditions at the stated T

composition.other_species: salt named in the label row (composition.salt): NaCl, KCl, CaCl2; single-salt solutions in doubly distilled degassed water. Column header is just 'm'; unit 'moles/kg H2O' is from the figure axes (Figs. 2, 3).

conversion_needs: psi to Pa; dP is differential, absolute brine pressure needs the pure-water saturation pressure at T (ITS not stated)
notes: Stacked layout: the printed table has NaCl, KCl and CaCl2 blocks side by side for each temperature; stacked here per temperature in the order NaCl, KCl, CaCl2. Table header column 'T (C)' holds the temperature printed once per block; it is set from label rows. Table continues on journal p. 673 (PDF page 6): KCl 275 C 4.6/126.7 and CaCl2 275 C rows 4.0-5.8 are on p. 673 while the rest of the 275 C blocks are on p. 672. Replicate molalities printed as is (CaCl2 325 C 5.3 twice, 6.1 twice; 350 C 5.5 twice). CaCl2 350 C: dP 537.0 at 6.4 is followed by 528.1 at 6.5 (non-monotonic, as printed). Authors state molality accuracy +-2.0 percent (NaCl, KCl) and +-5.0 percent (CaCl2); NaCl data below 325 C were used only as spot checks (paper text, p. 677).
quality_remarks: audit 2026-10-02: Three printed low-molality rows lie more than 3 psid below their neighbours while the stated systematic error is 1-2 psid: CSV row 1 (NaCl 200 C, 0.5 m, dP 0.8; about 4-5 psi expected from KCl 4.9 and NaCl 225 C 4.7), row 18 (CaCl2 200 C, 0.5 m, dP 1.9; about 6-7 expected), row 145 (CaCl2 300 C, 0.5 m, dP 11.5; KCl 22.7 and NaCl 17.7 at the same m, CaCl2 should be higher than NaCl). Kept as printed (page images checked). Differential pressure convention: dP = P_water - P_brine (text p.671: brine side low-pressure, water side high-pressure). NaCl rows below 325 C were used only as spot checks in the authors' fits. builder 2026-10-02: dP = P(pure water) - P(solution); the solution pressure is IAPWS-95 psat(T) minus dP.
caution: CSV rows 1, 18 and 145 (0.5 m NaCl 200 C, CaCl2 200 C, CaCl2 300 C) are more than 3 psid below neighbours (stated systematic error 1-2 psid); printed as is. dP = P_water - P_brine.
